markdown_report:
At 10% research progress, prioritize a controlled diagnostic improvement before changing SASRec. The selected idea is a **matched history intervention audit** that distinguishes item identity, ordering, and deletion-compaction sensitivity.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Electronics has the highest supplied sampled wrong-rank rate, 14.95%. This motivates category-specific investigation but does not establish its validation HR@10. (2) Current deletions change both content and positions. Their effects therefore cannot identify which change drives the response. (3) User feedback describes broad associations and disproportionate influence from occasional interests. These are hypotheses to investigate; histories alone cannot establish immediate usefulness or satisfied needs.

**Insights from related work.** (1) The recency study [1] motivates measuring dependence on recent interactions. It does not imply that stronger or weaker recency dependence always improves accuracy. (2) The supplied benchmark study [2] motivates last-item and additive-history references. Such comparisons can reveal whether apparent sequence sensitivity exceeds simpler predictive mechanisms. (3) Sampling reliability research [3] distinguishes discrimination from ranking fidelity. Two-candidate margins therefore require validation against the pinned selection metric.

**Directions and conceptual framework.** Organize research along three axes: intervention control, predictive reference models, and diagnostic validation. The following framework separates what each comparison measures:

| Comparison | Preserved | Investigated |
|---|---|---|
| Identity substitution | Length, occupied positions, latest item | Dependence on older identities |
| Prefix permutation | Item multiset, occupied positions, latest item | Dependence on older ordering |
| Deletion versus substitution | Edited source positions and count | Compaction-associated differences |
| Last-item/additive references | Targets and candidates | Need for richer history modeling |

These comparisons characterize model behavior; they do not identify causal preferences.

**Candidate ideas and assessments.** Scores are originality/potential/code difficulty, each out of 10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Matched intervention audit [1–3]: 5/8/4.** Originality: useful combination, established components. Potential: reusable architecture comparisons, uncertain connection to HR@10. Difficulty: existing hooks suffice, careful matching is required.
- **Last-item/additive score mixture [2]: 3/7/5.** Originality: direct reference-model integration, familiar construction. Potential: inexpensive predictive gains, possibly redundant with SASRec. Difficulty: small scoring modules, training and predictor synchronization required.
- **Diagnostic-to-validation concordance study [3,4]: 5/8/6.** Originality: explicitly tests diagnostic usefulness, standard association methods. Potential: improves later search decisions, few trials limit inference. Difficulty: simple statistics, substantial experiment cost.

**Selected algorithm.** Extend the existing persisted panel with fixed-position substitutions and prefix permutations, using five paired draws and unchanged-input controls. Match substitution items by training-frequency bin, exclude padding and the complete observed training history, and report unmatched cases. Freeze each target and negative across conditions; summarize paired margin changes, ordering flips, intervention strength, and eligible counts per category. Preserve existing deletion measurements but label their contrast with substitution descriptive because replacement adds different content. Keep all four categories and select models exclusively by pinned macro validation HR@10. Run bounded diagnostics within the shared budget; report uncertainty as conditional on the fitted checkpoint.

idea.description: Extend the paired history-sensitivity adapter with matched fixed-position substitutions and multiset-preserving prefix permutations. Compare these with existing deletions to distinguish sensitivity to older item identities, older ordering, and changes associated with compaction, without claiming causal identification.
idea.motivation: The supplied diagnostic workflow explicitly lacks positional controls, while qualitative feedback raises hypotheses about older and occasional interests. At 10% progress, improving interpretability of existing measurements is more feasible than committing to a new architecture. Supplied training-prefix margins identify Electronics as a useful investigation stratum, but no validation improvement is established.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Use the persisted training-only panel and view.model as authoritative; preserve model modes, RNG states, and buffer checks. Score through architecture-compatible view.log2feats and view.predict_score; preserve the explicit final_BD contract when applicable. For eligible prefixes with at least two older items, select older positions while holding the latest item fixed. Replace selected identities with distinct category-catalog items from the same training-frequency bin, excluding the user's complete training history and fixed candidates; report matching failures rather than silently relaxing constraints. Permutations preserve occupied positions and the item multiset; report changed-ID fractions because repeats can produce ineffective edits. Keep existing deletion conditions separate from the matched older-prefix comparison. Report metric formulas, requested and eligible counts, actual perturbation strength, and conditional paired-user intervals. An unchanged-input control measures deterministic repeatability. Training-prefix results remain in-sample diagnostics, and substitution introduces replacement content, so deletion contrasts do not isolate a pure positional effect. Preserve the twenty-user full-catalog unseen-item recommendation requirement, five users per category. Do not infer ownership, compatibility, immediate usefulness, or unobserved simulator traits from interaction IDs. Preserve dataset routing, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and the SASREC_EPOCHS environment default of 200. This diagnostic-only change requires no predictor architecture change; any later model modification must update the predictor writer.

originality.positive: Combines matched identity edits, order controls, and existing deletion probes within a reproducible architecture-aware diagnostic interface.
originality.negative: The interventions and paired comparisons are established techniques; their integration is the main contribution.

future_potential.positive: Provides reusable measurements for deciding whether subsequent architectures use history in meaningfully different ways.
future_potential.negative: Sensitivity measurements may have little association with validation HR@10, and replacement content prevents clean attribution of deletion contrasts.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses the existing panel, scoring hooks, RNG isolation, and aggregation machinery without retraining.
code_difficulty.negative: Frequency matching, repeated-item permutations, eligibility accounting, and architecture-compatible scoring require careful implementation.

related_work.title: [1] Measuring Recency Bias (2024)
contributions: Introduces a recency measurement and reports accuracy improvements after mitigating excessive recent-item emphasis, according to the supplied research summary.
Motivates explicit controls for which parts of history influence predictions.
limitations: Does not establish that recency sensitivity is inherently harmful or predict gains on these four datasets.

related_work.title: [2] Do Sequential Recommendation Benchmarks Require Higher-Order Sequence Modelling? (2026)
contributions: The supplied summary reports pairwise history models outperforming SASRec/eSASRec reproductions on four of five datasets.
Motivates last-item and additive-history reference models.
limitations: Results do not establish the same ordering under the pinned RecHarness splits and candidate sampling.

related_work.title: [3] On the Reliability of Sampling Strategies (RecSys 2025)
contributions: Distinguishes resolution, fidelity, robustness, and predictive power in sampled recommendation evaluation.
Motivates checking whether diagnostic changes correspond to the actual selection objective.
limitations: Does not validate two-candidate training-prefix margins as proxies for this task's validation HR@10.

related_work.title: [4] A Flexible Defense Against the Winner's Curse
contributions: Addresses inference after selecting an empirical winner, including dependent candidates.
Motivates logging all comparisons and distinguishing fixed-comparison uncertainty from adaptive selection uncertainty.
limitations: Ordinary paired-user bootstrap intervals do not automatically implement its selection-aware inference or capture training-seed variability.
